footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net loss: includes a $130M income tax benefit. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) fell 86.7% to $103M in 2025. Net interest income rose 14.4% to $719M and noninterest income was −$616M, versus $147M; noninterest expense rose 1.3%, and the provision for credit losses was $65.8M, versus $46.8M.
Net loss was −$398M, versus $153M, or −$2.95 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 547.4% versus 71.9%. Simmons First returned $115M through dividends.
sources: Simmons First National Corporation Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
